items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: And one night, my piano player don't show -- Clyde Hart.

ctx.x: No. The first record was "Poor(?) But Happy." And it was a little hit. Because the guys used to come home from the road and say, "Man, you got a hit out there." They'd heard it. It was an instrumental. So I got a chance to take the small band into Zanzibar. And I had already opened my studio teaching. So I had this little band, and I was doing good.

And one night, my piano player don't show -- Clyde Hart. And I didn't have nothin' but a piano and drums; I didn't have no guitar or nothin'. Piano, drums and bass. Because I didn't have about five or six pieces. And he don't show up. And that just killed my band. Because the least he could have done is got somebody... Because he had a recording date. See, Clyde Hart was the first piano player that got away from oom-pah. He was the first one to do that chord thing, you know. And he was very popular in recording.…
